why: Macworld (best-docks guide plus a hands-on Brydge Trio review) and Tom's Hardware both cover this. Their dock guides list specs and prices, and Tom's Hardware's guide names a 2.5GbE pick (Amazon Basics TB4 Pro). So major reviewers answer it in part. But they are general dock guides that are not filtered for 2.5GbE, and neither shows measured Ethernet throughput. Tom's Guide only covers a gigabit dock. The rest are listicles, a spec-only niche ranking, off-target pages and one blank page. A focused 2.5GbE page could get in, but it would be competing with Macworld and Tom's Hardware.
